newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures stuck in tight range.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures stuck in tight range.

text.p: Key three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures followed a rise in Japanese government bonds shortly before the close on Wednesday, after being frozen in a tight range in light trade throughout the session.

Dealers said the market lacked incentives to venture in any direction, as the general election scheduled on October 20 posed uncertainty over the outlook of the future shape of the government and its economic policy, dealers said.

Many dealers said buying of the March has become difficult after the recent rally took it to the level where the market has almost completely ruled out any possibility of a rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) until the spring.

"99.35 seems to be the limit the March can go at best," said a dealer at a city bank. On the other hand, expectations that interest rates will remain at current low levels at least until the end of this year could thwart any movements toward the downside, dealers said.
The result was the March contract's tight daily range of between 99.31 and 99.33 and small volume of 15,344 contracts.
Having found the March stalled at current levels, market players are starting to look at the June contract more and more, some dealers said.
The June contract's trade volume exceeded the March for the first time on Wednesday at 20,607 contracts.
In the interbank market, the key unsecured overnight call rate was mostly traded at 0.45 percent, steady from Tuesday.
The BOJ's regular money market operation was neutral as expected. It injected 100 billion yen to offset a fund shortfall of 90 billion yen.
Rates were steady in the open market, too, with key three-month certificates of deposit issued at an unchanged 0.52 percent. About 150 billion yen worth of issues have been detected.

About 10 billion worth of two-month CDs was issued at 0.50 percent, the same rate as Tuesday. The one-month CD rate was also steady at 0.49 percent, with about 50 billion yen worth of CDs issued. The market is likely to remain steady for a while as nothing seems to change the market's view that the Japanese economy's recovery is slow, the dealer said.
